entities.summary: Olayinka Koso-Thomas who was born in 1937 is a Nigerian-born doctor who lives in Sierra Leone. She is internationally recognised for her efforts to abolish female genital cutting. In 1998, she shared a Prince of Asturias Award for her work. Her study of the practice in Sierra Leone highlights its important role in the traditional initiations of females into both womanhood and society in parts of West Africa.
